subtitle: A brief alphabetized glossary of Internet and OSI terms prepared for Interop 90.

tldr.problem: Readers at an interoperability conference encountered many networking terms and acronyms from Internet and OSI systems.

sections.title: The Interop Pocket Glossary
sections.content:
RFC 1208 adapts the INTEROP Pocket Glossary of Networking Terms, which was distributed at Interop 90. It was intended to help readers understand the terminology and acronyms used at the tutorials, conference, and exhibition.

The editors kept definitions brief and omitted familiar computer and communications words. They recommend networking textbooks for more complete explanations and invite suggestions for future editions.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo reprints a small glossary made for a networking event. It gives short explanations and leaves common computer terms out.

sections.title: Internet and OSI Vocabulary
sections.content:
The alphabetical entries cover both Internet protocol terms and the OSI networking model. Examples include ARP, DNS, TCP, UDP, SNMP, MIB, and router, alongside OSI terms such as ACSE, CLNP, and X.400.

Many entries point readers to related terms. The glossary's short definitions are intended as an introduction rather than a complete technical treatment.
sections.plainLanguage: The entries cover words from Internet and OSI networking. Many entries direct readers to another related term.

sections.title: Examples of Definitions
sections.content:
The glossary defines a maximum transmission unit as the largest data unit that can be sent on a physical medium, and gives Ethernet at 1500 bytes as an example. It describes a router as a system that selects among paths using routing information and metrics.

It also includes an intentionally playful entry for Bart Simpson and notes that the term interoperability was left undefined because its meaning was still unsettled among the authors.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples show how the memo defines technical terms and records the authors' uncertainty about one word. It also includes a playful entry.

sections.title: Networking Words in Their Time
sections.content:
The glossary describes gateway as an earlier Internet term for what it calls a router, or more precisely an IP router. It says that modern use of gateway and application gateway refers to systems that translate between formats, such as mail systems.

The authors note that networking terms change rapidly and describe the glossary as a moving target. The memo's security section says security issues are not discussed.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo shows that networking terms can change their meanings over time. It describes gateway as an older name for an IP router.
